newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-SPARTA-AJAX POSTPONED AMID FEARS OF VIOLENCE. [CORRECTED 20:57 GMT]
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPARTA-AJAX POSTPONED AMID FEARS OF VIOLENCE. [CORRECTED 20:57 GMT]

text.p: The Dutch soccer association has postponed next Sunday's scheduled match between Sparta Rotterdam and Ajax Amsterdam for fear of hooligan violence involving Ajax and Feyenoord Rotterdam fans, the Dutch ANP news agency said on Monday.

Police and the Rotterdam authorities believed bands of followers of Ajax and their traditional arch-rivals Feyenoord had arranged a confrontation on the day of the match, ANP said (corrects to make clear that the violence was not expected between Ajax and Sparta fans).
A match between Ajax and Feyenoord in Amsterdam on Sunday passed largely without incident.
But Dutch newspapers said on Monday that hooligan leaders were planning fights next Sunday and had used the Internet communications network to arrange the clashes.
They were hoping to take advantage of a lighter police presence at the Sparta-Ajax match, which has no history of hooliganism.

At Sunday's Ajax-Feyenoord game, the Feyenoord fans were under heavy police guard. Police did, however, make 11 arrests, largely of Ajax supporters, while a group of Feyenoord fans started a small fire in the stadium.
A week before, fans clashed on a ringroad north of Amsterdam as a Feyenoord convoy passed by.
Feyenoord are at home on Saturday. No new date has yet been set for the postponed Sparta-Ajax game.
